title: Caffeine can still be active up to eight hours later
summary: NHLBI says caffeine is a stimulant that can interfere with sleep, and that its effects can last up to eight hours.
body: The habits page groups nicotine and caffeine as stimulants that can interfere with sleep. On caffeine, it says the effects can last up to 8 hours, so a cup of coffee in the late afternoon can make it hard to fall asleep at night. The examples it lists include caffeinated soda, coffee, tea, and chocolate. The eight-hour line is about the substance, not a ban written for one child. The page is US guidance on habits, not a dose chart.

sources.title: Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency: Healthy Sleep Habits
